content.text:
Complete map of the `libghostty-spm` / `GhosttyKit` dependency.

---

## 1. Where the dependency is declared / pinned

**`macapp/project.yml` — package declaration (the single source of truth):**
- `macapp/project.yml:48-55` — package `libghostty`, `url: https://github.com/Lakr233/libghostty-spm`, `exactVersion: 1.2.3`. Comment (lines 49-53):
  > "Prebuilt GhosttyKit.xcframework (the libghostty C API as a static archive) distributed as a Swift package. We link the `GhosttyKit` product (raw C API) and roll our own terminal surface view — NOT the higher-level `GhosttyTerminal` wrapper. The embedding API is not yet stable, so pin EXACT. Pre-GA we move to a self-built xcframework from a Ghostty fork for full pin/patch control (see plan CMT-2)."
- `macapp/project.yml:182-186` — the **only** target linking it: `WorkroomApp` → `- package: libghostty / product: GhosttyKit`. Comment: "Its package links c++ + Carbon; the static Ghostty archive additionally needs these system frameworks at final link (GPU renderer + CoreText font backend + HID)."
- `macapp/project.yml:224-228` — the system frameworks added *for* GhosttyKit: `Metal.framework`, `MetalKit.framework`, `CoreText.framework`, `IOKit.framework`, `QuartzCore.framework`.
- `macapp/project.yml:153-156` — bundled runtime resources folder reference (see §3).

**Package.resolved** — `macapp/WorkroomApp.xcodeproj/project.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/swiftpm/Package.resolved` is **gitignored** (`.gitignore:16` ignores the whole `/macapp/WorkroomApp.xcodeproj/`). The local working copy pins:
```
"identity": "libghostty-spm", "kind": "remoteSourceControl",
"location": "https://github.com/Lakr233/libghostty-spm",
"revision": "df168f41e5a22b319c184e40f021895746ad4e8f", "version": "1.2.3"
```
So the version pin in git is **only** `project.yml`; nothing else pins the resolved revision.

**Makefile / Scripts:**
- Root `Makefile:44` — `APP_XCODEBUILD` includes `-derivedDataPath DerivedData -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages`, i.e. the xcframework is resolved into `macapp/DerivedData/SourcePackages/` and reused. `Makefile:79, 82, 85, 91` run `xcodegen generate` before each build; `Makefile:107` (`app-clean`) removes `DerivedData` + the `.xcodeproj`, which forces a re-download.
- `macapp/Scripts/build-helper.sh` — **no** ghostty references at all (it only builds/embeds/signs the Go CLI).
- `macapp/Scripts/release.sh:99` — `-clonedSourcePackagesDirPath "$BUILD/SourcePackages"` (same SPM checkout mechanism); line 189 only greps SourcePackages for Sparkle's `sign_update`. No ghostty-specific handling — the static archive is linked into the main executable so there is nothing extra to sign.
- **`macapp/Scripts/run.sh` does not exist.** `macapp/CLAUDE.md` ("Layout" section) still documents `Scripts/` as containing "`run.sh` (local)" — stale doc reference. The actual local loop is `make app-run` (`Makefile:68`).

**CI (`.github/workflows/`):**
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:151-163` — "Cache SPM packages": caches `macapp/DerivedData/SourcePackages` keyed on `hashFiles('macapp/project.yml')`, `restore-keys: spm-${{ runner.os }}-`. Comment: "SPM resolves ~15 packages (Sparkle, Sentry, **libghostty**, the tree-sitter grammars, and swift-syntax pulled transitively) by cloning them from GitHub on every run… so an unchanged set skips the network entirely."
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:165-186` — "Cache Xcode build dir": caches `macapp/DerivedData/Build` keyed on Xcode version + `project.yml` hash (this is where `libghostty.a` / `GhosttyKit.swiftmodule` land).
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:197-209` — "Resolve SPM packages (retry on network flake)": `xcodegen generate` then up to 3× `xcodebuild -resolvePackageDependencies` with `-clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages`. Skipped on an exact cache hit.
- `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` and `.github/workflows/release.yml` have **no SPM/DerivedData caching at all** — they resolve libghostty from GitHub cold on every run (`nightly.yml:140`, `release.yml:59` only `brew install xcodegen …`).

---

## 2. The C API surface we consume

**Counts (over `macapp/WorkroomApp/`, excluding tests):**
- **61 distinct `ghostty_*` identifiers** (functions + types + struct/union types). One extra token, `ghostty_surface_` at `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalCaptureSupport.swift:4`, is a doc-comment glob, not a symbol.
- **41 distinct `GHOSTTY_*` C enum constants** (the raw grep yields 43 including the doc-comment fragment `GHOSTTY_ACTION_` at `TerminalSearch.swift` and the env-var *string* `GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR`).
- `import GhosttyKit` appears in exactly **3 files**: `Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:3`, `Core/GhosttyApp.swift:3`, `Core/GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.swift:3`. Every other reference is a comment/doc mention.

**Main consumers (reference counts):**

| File | refs |
|---|---|
| `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift` | 131 |
| `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttyApp.swift` | 40 |
| `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.swift` | 29 |
| `Core/TerminalSearch.swift` (4), `Core/TerminalLinkOpener.swift` (4), `Core/TerminalCaptureSupport.swift` (3), `Core/TerminalSessions.swift` (2), `WorkroomApp.swift` (1), `Core/WindowBackgroundThemer.swift` (1), `Core/QuickTerminalController.swift` (1), `Core/AppStore.swift` (1) | comments only |

### `Core/GhosttyApp.swift` — the runtime (app-level API)
Functions: `ghostty_init` (57), `ghostty_config_new` (188), `ghostty_config_load_file` (189), `ghostty_config_finalize` (190), `ghostty_config_free` (95, 212, 286), `ghostty_app_new` (93), `ghostty_app_set_color_scheme` (101, 264), `ghostty_app_set_focus` (121, 134), `ghostty_app_update_config` (209), `ghostty_app_tick` (256), `ghostty_app_free` (281), `ghostty_info` (110).
Types: `ghostty_app_t` (26, 120), `ghostty_config_t` (28), `ghostty_runtime_config_s` (67), `ghostty_color_scheme_e` (267), `ghostty_surface_t` (via signature).
Constants: `GHOSTTY_SUCCESS` (57), `GHOSTTY_COLOR_SCHEME_DARK`/`_LIGHT` (264, 268).
Runtime callback struct fields assigned at 68-91: `userdata`, `supports_selection_clipboard`, `wakeup_cb`, `action_cb`, `read_clipboard_cb`, `confirm_read_clipboard_cb`, `write_clipboard_cb`, `close_surface_cb`.

### `Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift` — the surface (per-terminal API), 40 distinct functions/types
Lifecycle/config: `ghostty_surface_config_new` (205), `ghostty_platform_u`/`ghostty_platform_macos_s` (207-208), `ghostty_env_var_s` (122, 230), `ghostty_surface_new` (245), `ghostty_surface_free` (296, 331), `ghostty_surface_update_config` (536), `ghostty_surface_t` (19).
Geometry/render: `ghostty_surface_set_content_scale` (252, 356), `ghostty_surface_set_size` (253, 363), `ghostty_surface_set_display_id` (258, 360), `ghostty_surface_set_occlusion` (449).
Focus/theme: `ghostty_surface_set_focus` (490), `ghostty_surface_set_color_scheme` (529).
Text read: `ghostty_surface_has_selection` (748), `ghostty_surface_read_selection` (750), `ghostty_surface_read_text` (786, 805), `ghostty_surface_free_text` (751, 787, 806, 1276), `ghostty_surface_quicklook_word` (1275), `ghostty_text_s`, `ghostty_selection_s`, `ghostty_point_s`.
Write/input: `ghostty_surface_text` (815, 1492), `ghostty_surface_key` (851, 855, 868, 891, 910, 915, 924, 939, 957), `ghostty_surface_preedit` (1169, 1171), `ghostty_surface_ime_point` (1539), `ghostty_surface_key_translation_mods` (1124), `ghostty_input_key_s` (1079), `ghostty_input_mods_e` (1097, 1117), `ghostty_input_action_e` (838, 935), `ghostty_input_scroll_mods_t` (1266).
Mouse: `ghostty_surface_mouse_pos` (1186, 1211, 1223, 1235, 1259), `ghostty_surface_mouse_button` (1198, 1212, 1236, 1247, 1260), `ghostty_surface_mouse_scroll` (1268).
Other: `ghostty_surface_process_exited` (703), `ghostty_surface_binding_action` (1069).
Constants: `GHOSTTY_PLATFORM_MACOS`, `GHOSTTY_SURFACE_CONTEXT_TAB`, `GHOSTTY_ACTION_PRESS/RELEASE/REPEAT`, all 10 `GHOSTTY_MODS_*`, `GHOSTTY_MOUSE_PRESS/RELEASE/LEFT/RIGHT`, `GHOSTTY_POINT_SCREEN/SURFACE/COORD_TOP_LEFT/COORD_BOTTOM_RIGHT`, `GHOSTTY_COLOR_SCHEME_*`.

### `Core/GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.swift` — the callback surface
Functions: `ghostty_surface_userdata` (151), `ghostty_surface_complete_clipboard_request` (192).
Types in callback signatures: `ghostty_app_t`, `ghostty_target_s`, `ghostty_action_s`, `ghostty_action_open_url_s`, `ghostty_action_command_finished_s`, `ghostty_clipboard_e`, `ghostty_clipboard_content_s`, `ghostty_clipboard_request_e`.
Union field accesses (the most ABI-fragile part): `action.action.pwd.pwd`, `.set_title.title`, `.command_finished.exit_code`, `.progress_report.state`, `.desktop_notification.title/.body`, `.open_url.url/.len`, `.mouse_over_link.url/.len`, `.scrollbar.total/.offset/.len`, `.child_exited.exit_code`, `.start_search.needle`, `.search_total.total`, `.search_selected.selected`; plus `target.tag` / `target.target.surface`.

### Enum switches (the API-bump breakage points)
- **`GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.handleAction`, `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.swift:25`** — `switch action.tag { … }` over `ghostty_action_e`, matching **14** cases (`PWD`, `SET_TITLE`, `COMMAND_FINISHED`, `PROGRESS_REPORT`, `DESKTOP_NOTIFICATION`, `OPEN_URL`, `MOUSE_OVER_LINK`, `SCROLLBAR`, `SHOW_CHILD_EXITED`, `START_SEARCH`, `END_SEARCH`, `SEARCH_TOTAL`, `SEARCH_SELECTED`, `RING_BELL`). It is **NOT exhaustive** — it has a `default:` at line 127 returning `false` (comment: "Tab/split/window intents, child-exit, and everything else are intentionally not handled… returning false lets libghostty fall back to its default"). So a new/renumbered action tag degrades silently rather than failing to compile.
- No other switch in the three GhosttyKit-importing files is over a C enum (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:1041` and `:1140` switch on `NSEvent.keyCode`).
- Raw-value arithmetic on `ghostty_input_mods_e` at `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:1094-1098` and `1104-1118` (`.rawValue |=` then `ghostty_input_mods_e(rawValue:)`), plus hardcoded AppKit right-modifier bitmasks at `1100-1102`. `translatedOptionAsAlt` (1122-1126) masks `GHOSTTY_MODS_ALT.rawValue` off the value `ghostty_surface_key_translation_mods` returns.
- `GHOSTTY_PROGRESS_STATE_REMOVE` inequality test at `GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.swift:57` — everything not-REMOVE is treated as "working".
- `TerminalCaptureSupport.swift:11-14` encodes the `Int16` / `-1` sentinel contract of `ghostty_action_command_finished_s.exit_code`.
- `TerminalSearch.swift:39-47` and `:70-84` hardcode the libghostty **keybind-action strings** (`start_search`, `search:<needle>`, `navigate_search:next|previous`, `end_search`) passed as raw C strings to `ghostty_surface_binding_action` — a string API with no compile-time checking at all.

---

## 3. Bundled runtime resources

**Contents of `macapp/Resources/ghostty/` — 66 tracked files:**
- `SOURCE.md` (1019 B)
- `terminfo/67/ghostty` and `terminfo/78/xterm-ghostty` (compiled terminfo, 3.8 KB each)
- `shell-integration/` — `bash/bash-preexec.sh`, `bash/ghostty.bash`, `elvish/lib/ghostty-integration.elv`, `fish/vendor_conf.d/ghostty-shell-integration.fish`, `nushell/vendor/autoload/ghostty.nu`, `zsh/.zshenv`, `zsh/ghostty-integration`
- `themes/` — **56 entries**: 54 upstream Ghostty theme files + `LICENSE` (MIT) + the two hand-authored `Workroom` / `Workroom Light` files added in `8fd7fa19`.

**How it reaches the bundle:** `macapp/project.yml:153-156` — a **folder reference** source entry:
```yaml
- path: Resources/ghostty
  type: folder
  buildPhase: resources
```
Comment: "libghostty runtime resources (terminfo + shell-integration). Folder reference so the tree (e.g. terminfo/78/xterm-ghostty) is copied verbatim into Contents/Resources/ghostty; GhosttyApp points GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR at it. See Resources/ghostty/SOURCE.md."

**Provenance / version marker — `macapp/Resources/ghostty/SOURCE.md`:**
> "The `libghostty-spm` package ships NO resources, so these are vendored. **Sourced from a recent Ghostty build.** **TODO (pre-GA, CMT-2):** when we move to a self-built xcframework from a pinned Ghostty fork, regenerate these from that exact tag so they version-match the binary. Themes are intentionally omitted (Workroom themes via macOS system colors, not Ghostty themes)."

Two things to note: there is **no version/ref/commit marker anywhere** — "a recent Ghostty build" is the entire provenance record; and the last sentence is now **factually stale**, since `themes/` was added afterwards by `8fd7fa19` and `602b5aa3` (issue #36) and is load-bearing for the theme picker.

**Runtime readers of these paths:**
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttyApp.swift:150-178` (`resolveResources`) — resolves `Bundle.main.resourceURL/ghostty`, gates on `shell-integration` existing, `setenv("GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR", …, 1)` at :159, and separately probes `terminfo/78/xterm-ghostty` at :168-171 to set `terminfoDirectory`. Missing shell-integration → fail-soft ("bundled ghostty resources not found — terminals unavailable", Sentry `.error`); missing terminfo → Sentry `.warning` only.
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:220-234` — injects `TERMINFO=<terminfoDirectory>` into the surface config's `env_vars` array (a process-level `setenv` does not reach the child).
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ThemeService.swift:164-171` (`themeDirectories`) — `~/.config/ghostty/themes` **first** (wins), then `Bundle.main.resourceURL/ghostty/themes`; read by `themePreview(named:)` (:150-162) and `parseThemeFile` (:175+). `ThemeService.families` (:38-…) hardcodes 22 family names whose variant strings must match filenames in that dir.
- `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttyApp.swift:225-240` (`writeThemeConfig`) — writes `theme = "<name>"` into `~/Library/Application Support/Workroom/ghostty.conf`, which libghostty then resolves against `$GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR/themes`.

---

## 4. Workarounds attributed in a comment to a libghostty/GhosttyKit 1.2.3 limitation

There are exactly **four** comments in the shipped tree that name `1.2.3` (plus one in tests, one in UI tests). All others are attributed to "libghostty" generically.

### 4a. Backspace keycode — `filterSpecialCharacters` (the canonical 1.2.3 workaround)
- **`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:900-906`**, in `keyDown`. Exact comment:
  > "Derive text from `event.characters`, dropping AppKit sentinels (see `filterSpecialCharacters`): function keys / arrows resolve to "" here and fall through to the keycode-only branch, which libghostty encodes correctly. DEL (U+7F, the Backspace key) is intentionally KEPT and sent as text — **libghostty 1.2.3's *keycode* encoding for backspace is broken (it emits a space for the backspace keycode)**, but forwarding the literal 0x7f byte as text delivers the correct erase. (Confirmed by raw-PTY byte probing; matches Muxy's filter. **Revisit if we move off 1.2.3.**)"
- The implementation is `GhosttySurfaceView.filterSpecialCharacters` at **`:1158-1163`** — drops any string whose first scalar is `< 0x20` or in `0xF700…0xF8FF`, and deliberately keeps `0x7F`. Doc comment at `:1150-1157`.
- The same filter is applied on the control-only path at **`:848`**.
- Pinned by test: **`macapp/WorkroomAppTests/GhosttySurfaceViewTests.swift:36-40`** — "The backspace fix: DEL (0x7F) must be forwarded as text (libghostty 1.2.3 mis-encodes the backspace *keycode*, so we send the byte instead)."
- Cross-referenced in `TODOS.md:62-64`: "**Backspace keycode encoding** — 1.2.3 mis-encodes the backspace *keycode* (emits a space); we work around it by sending DEL as text (`GhosttySurfaceView.filterSpecialCharacters`). If the upgrade fixes the keycode path, the workaround can be simplified."
- Related but *not* 1.2.3-attributed: `GhosttyApp.swift:161-166` + `SOURCE.md:5-8` explain the `TERMINFO` injection also exists so Backspace works (missing `kbs` capability) — a resources gap, not an API bug.

### 4b. Run-command exit code — the exit-capture wrapper
- **This is now a `.status` file, not a `.exit` file.** The original EXIT-trap `.exit`-file wrapper was introduced in commit **`a489fb6b`** ("feat(macapp): detect run command success/failure (#79)"), whose message states: *"Root cause: **GhosttyKit 1.2.3 reports the child exit_code as 0 no matter the real code**, so failure never fired end-to-end… The run wrapper now records the command's real `$?` via an EXIT trap to a per-run `.exit` file"*. That commit's code carried comments reading "libghostty's child-exit code is unreliable in this embedding (**GhosttyKit 1.2.3 always reports 0**)".
- It was **replaced** by commit `98ecbe5b` ("fix(macapp): run command under an in-terminal supervisor (issue #7)"). Today the mechanism is:
  - `macapp/Resources/run-supervisor/supervisor.sh:29-32` (`write_status`, atomic temp+rename), `:83-105` — writes `starting` / `running <pid>` / `stopping` / `stopped` / `exited <code>` to the status file; `:103` `write_status "exited $code"` is the real-exit-code capture.
  - `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1572-1576` — `supervisorStatusPath(forPidPath:)` derives `<pid path>.status`.
  - `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1749-1784` — `applyRunStatus` parses the line into `RunState`/`RunOutcome`.
  - `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:2118-2144` — `markRunExited`. Comment at `:2121-2123`: *"Prefer the supervisor's final status line (authoritative — it wrote `stopped`/`exited <code>` just before exiting) **over libghostty's unreliable exit code**, in case the poller hadn't read it yet when this child-exit callback fired."* — this is the surviving in-code attribution, but it says "unreliable", **not** "1.2.3".
- The only surviving **version-attributed** comment for this workaround is in a test: **`macapp/WorkroomAppUITests/RunStatusUITests.swift:5-7`**:
  > "a real non-zero exit → the failed run icon (the wrapper records the code; **libghostty's own child-exit code is unreliable in GhosttyKit 1.2.3**, so this proves the recorded-code path)."

### 4c. Theme application
- **`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttyApp.swift:226-230`**, in `writeThemeConfig`. Exact comment:
  > "libghostty resolves `theme = "<name>"` from $GHOSTTY_RESOURCES_DIR/themes (and ~/.config/ghostty/themes, which wins) — **verified on GhosttyKit 1.2.3 for new and live surfaces.**"
- The workaround itself is at **`GhosttyApp.swift:215-240`**: *"libghostty has no config setter API (only load-from-file), so Workroom's 'blend into the native window' look is expressed as a tiny generated config file"* — the app writes `~/Library/Application Support/Workroom/ghostty.conf` and reloads it (`reloadConfig` at `:201-213`, `ghostty_app_update_config` + per-surface `ghostty_surface_update_config` at `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:534-537`). This is a "no setter API" limitation, version-verified against 1.2.3.

### 4d. Inline-agent capture boundary
- **`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:775-776`**, doc comment on `readCommandRegion`:
  > "**The exact command-start boundary isn't exposed by libghostty 1.2.3**; reading the active screen captures recent output (errors live at the end), and the host trims/caps via `TerminalCapture`."
- The workaround is `readCommandRegion` (`:777-790`) reading the whole `GHOSTTY_POINT_SCREEN` rect instead of an OSC-133 command region, plus `TerminalCapture.tidy` tail-capping in `Core/TerminalCaptureSupport.swift:23-42`.

### 4e. Engine-init test assertion
- **`macapp/WorkroomAppTests/GhosttyAppTests.swift:11-13`** — `XCTAssertTrue(GhosttyApp.shared.isReady, "libghostty failed to initialize — check bundled ghostty resources and **the 1.2.3 C API**")`.

### Workarounds attributed to libghostty but **NOT** to a version (relevant to the same blast radius)

- **Ctrl-Tab / `isAppShortcut`** — `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:966-1031`. The doc at `:975-980`: *"This list is load-bearing and easy to forget: a menu shortcut that ISN'T here reaches the terminal, and a TUI in an enhanced keyboard mode (Claude/Codex) consumes it, so the menu's key equivalent never fires. That has shipped as a bug twice (most recently issue #128), which is why it now has tests."* ⌃Tab/⌥Tab are deliberately **excluded** — `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/QuickSwitcher.swift:70`, `macapp/WorkroomApp/WorkroomApp.swift:282`, and the `macapp/CLAUDE.md` "Gotchas" bullet; pinned by `macapp/WorkroomAppTests/AppShortcutReservationTests.swift`. Also `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:1033-1050` (`handleScrollKeyEquivalent`): *"libghostty has no default binding for these, so we intercept them before forwarding the keystroke."*
- **OSC 99 / desktop notifications** — no code workaround exists. `GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.swift:61-68` handles `GHOSTTY_ACTION_DESKTOP_NOTIFICATION` (OSC 9 / 777 only). The gap is documented in `macapp/QA-libghostty.md:73-80` and `TODOS.md:54-61` (see §5).
- **Focus reporting / `ghostty_app_set_focus`** — `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttyApp.swift:102-108`: *"Real Ghostty's macOS app drives this from NSApplication activation; **we were missing it entirely** — only per-surface `ghostty_surface_set_focus` (from first-responder changes) was wired. The gap surfaces as a terminal focus desync: a focus-tracking TUI (Claude Code, Codex) can end up stuck ignoring navigation keys after the app/terminal loses and regains focus… a prerequisite for correct DECSET 1004 (`CSI I`/`CSI O`) focus reporting."* Implemented at `:120-135` (`observeAppFocus`/`setAppFocus`). Companion de-dup guard at `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:478-491` (`lastSetFocus`, "without this guard, two triggers landing on the same value would emit a duplicate DECSET-1004 focus report to the TUI"), plus `syncFocusToKeyWindow` (`:493-502`) and `adoptFocusIfFirstResponder` (`:513-523`).
- **Surface free / teardown races** — four sites:
  - `macapp/WorkroomApp/WorkroomApp.swift:606-616` — *"Deliberately does NOT tear down libghostty on quit. Freeing surfaces (or the app) while their IO/render is still active races libghostty's surface teardown and crashes — **EXC_BAD_ACCESS in `Surface.deinit`, or `os_unfair_lock` corruption in `Surface.handleMessage`** — most readily when a run command's dev server (issue #7) is still busy."* `applicationWillTerminate` is an empty body (`:620`).
  - `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/QuickTerminalController.swift:89-95` — *"This fires from a libghostty action callback, so defer the teardown off that stack: **freeing a surface synchronously inside a libghostty callback races its IO and crashes**"* → `DispatchQueue.main.async { self?.close() }`.
  - `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:1240-1249` — after `popUpContextMenu`, *"Re-read `self.surface` rather than reusing the captured pointer: a context-menu command can free the surface during the modal (Close Terminal), and the balancing RELEASE on a freed surface is a **use-after-free crash**."*
  - `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:302-325` (`tearDown`) + `Core/TerminalSessions.swift:1333-1336` — callbacks nil'd before `ghostty_surface_free`, "so no in-flight libghostty callback touches a dead view"; plus the `isTornDown` / `canSpawnSurface` re-spawn guard (`:21-26`, `:189-195`).
- **Scrollback search wrap** — `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSearch.swift:63-66`: *"**Wrap is synthesized host-side:** libghostty's `navigate_search` does NOT wrap — the bundled Ghostty (**1.3.1**) stops dead at the ends ('we don't wrap or reset the match currently')."* Note the version conflict: `TerminalSearch.swift:5` and `:64` both assert the bundled engine is **Ghostty 1.3.x / 1.3.1**, while `project.yml` pins `libghostty-spm` **1.2.3** and `TODOS.md:32` states the packager is still on 1.2.3 while ghostty released 1.3.0/1.3.1. These two claims cannot both be right.
- **Scrollbar** — `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:130-132`: "libghostty draws none and exposes no scroll position to poll — it only pushes geometry via `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SCROLLBAR`."
- **No PTY child PID** — `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:95-97`: "the cwd source for ⌘-click path resolution — CMT-1, since **libghostty exposes no PTY child PID for `proc_pidinfo`**"; hence cwd is tracked purely from `GHOSTTY_ACTION_PWD` (`handlePwd`, `:656-661`; `Core/TerminalLinkOpener.swift:197-223`).
- **`wait_after_command` emits no close action** — `GhosttySurfaceView.swift:71-76` and `:830-837`: "libghostty shows the prompt but never emits a close action here, so close the tab ourselves on the next key."

---

## 5. Docs discussing the dependency / the plan to own it

**`TODOS.md:9-70` — "Own the GhosttyKit xcframework (macapp) — CMT-2", listed under "P1 — before GA".** The most complete statement:
- `:16` — "**Current state:** `macapp/project.yml` still pins `libghostty-spm` at `exactVersion: 1.2.3`."
- `:28-33` — "The embedding C API is explicitly unstable/internal ('breaking changes are expected'). **The packager already lags upstream.** ghostty has released **v1.3.0 and v1.3.1**, but libghostty-spm is still on **`1.2.3`** (published 2026-06-01; tags 1.2.1→1.2.3 only). So 'just use new libghostty-spm releases as they arrive' means trailing ghostty by ~2 versions on a single maintainer's cadence."
- `:24-27` — GA is itself a trigger: "shipping GA on a single-maintainer repackaging of an explicitly-unstable API is a **supply-chain risk**; owning the pin is the control."
- `:36-45` — the how: libghostty-spm's own `build.sh --source /path/to/ghostty`, "and **regenerate `terminfo`/`shell-integration` from that same ref** (fixes the SOURCE.md version-skew TODO)."
- `:47-48` — "**Depends on:** nothing in-app — it's a dependency-source swap (`macapp/project.yml`, `macapp/Resources/ghostty/`)."
- `:50-64` — **known gaps to recheck**: OSC 99 (no parser in any ghostty release *or* `main`; open PR ghostty-org/ghostty#10467) and the backspace keycode encoding.
- `TODOS.md:73-110` — CMT-3 (terminal *content* a11y) is explicitly sequenced *after* CMT-2; `:109-110` notes it depends on "the read APIs already present in 1.2.3 (`ghostty_surface_read_selection`, `ghostty_surface_read_text`, `extractString`)".

**`macapp/CLAUDE.md`** ("Gotchas"):
> "**The terminal is libghostty** (`libghostty-spm`'s `GhosttyKit` xcframework, pinned `exactVersion: 1.2.3` in project.yml). The embedding C API is not yet stable, so pin EXACT — don't float it. The terminal surface (`Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift`) + runtime (`GhosttyApp`/`GhosttyRuntimeAdapter`) are ours; the bundled `Resources/ghostty` (terminfo + shell-integration) must ship for the engine to start. Pre-GA, the plan is to move to a self-built xcframework from a pinned Ghostty fork."

Also in `macapp/CLAUDE.md` ("Dev tasks"): "Builds reuse `macapp/DerivedData/` so the Swift packages (incl. the GhosttyKit xcframework) aren't re-resolved/re-downloaded every build." And under the VCS core section: the WrVcs xcframework must be **library-only (no headers)** because "a headers-bearing static xcframework copies its `module.modulemap` into the shared `Debug/include/` and **collides with GhosttyKit's** ('Multiple commands produce include/module.modulemap')" — mirrored at `vcs/scripts/build-apple.sh:11` and `:124`.

**`macapp/README.md`:**
- `:141-143` — "**libghostty pin** (`project.yml`): `libghostty-spm`'s `GhosttyKit` xcframework pinned to `exactVersion: 1.2.3`. The embedding C API is not yet stable, so pin EXACT — don't float it. Pre-GA: move to a self-built xcframework from a pinned Ghostty fork. ✓ the app builds + links."
- `:144-146` — "**Terminal teardown**… ✓ frees the surface via `ghostty_surface_free` (callbacks cleared first). Still worth a runtime check: switch/delete workrooms repeatedly and confirm no orphaned shells in `ps`."
- `:4`, `:8`, `:50`, `:85` — architecture/build mentions.

**Root `README.md`:**
- `:120` — tech table: "**Terminal engine** | [libghostty](https://ghostty.org) (`libghostty-spm` **1.2.x**, Metal-rendered)".
- `:580` — "Key dependencies: **libghostty-spm** (terminal), …".
- `:827-828` — points at `macapp/CLAUDE.md` and `macapp/QA-libghostty.md`.

**`macapp/QA-libghostty.md`** — 135-line manual QA checklist for the SwiftTerm→libghostty migration (`b81d5c6d` + review fixes), 13 sections A–M. The parts stating a known gap:
- `:73-80` (§H): "**N/A OSC 99**: `printf '\e]99;;Hello from 99\a'` → **not supported by ghostty yet — it's coming.** Verified against ghostty `main`: no OSC-99 parser today (only OSC 9 / 777 notify; '99' → invalid and dropped), so it doesn't reach the app. But there's an **open upstream PR, ghostty-org/ghostty#10467**… So OSC 99 should work once we build the xcframework from a ghostty that includes #10467 (or cherry-pick it into our fork)… **SwiftTerm parsed OSC 99 itself, so this is a temporary minor regression.**"

- `:121-123` (§M): "it **wraps** at the ends… The wrap is synthesized host-side (**the engine doesn't wrap**), so verify it on a needle with **many** matches."
- `:64-67` (§G): "**Bell** 🔧 (critical regression — was silent)".
- `:110-113` (§L): OSC 52 read is "permissive default — deferred-policy item".

{"number":5634,"title":"OSC 99 style desktop notifications","body":"
### Discussed in https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/4405



<sup>Originally posted by **ehamiter** January  2, 2025</sup>
Coming from kitty, there's a nice way to implement desktop notifications, e.g.

```
printf '\x1b]99;;foo has been updated\x1b\\'
```

This makes it easy to add notifications to scripts, processes, etc. More info on how kitty implements it here:

https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/desktop-notifications/

Just curious if this would be something easy to implement or not.

Thank you!

{"number":12902,"title":"core: send selection_changed notification","body":"The core had no signal to the apprt when the active selection changed, so a consumer (e.g. a screen reader) kept reading a stale selection until some unrelated query refreshed it.

This change adds a payload-less selection_changed action that's fired on a selection state transition. The apprt reads the current selection through the normal read path.

This consolidates selection state changes so the notification fires consistently: all sites route through setSelection rather than calling screen.select directly, including the mouse paths that previously bypassed it for clipboard timing.

The new setSelectionAndCopy extends setSelection with the additional 'copy_on_select' behavior.

On macOS, this posts .ghosttySelectionDidChange, which is debounced before posting a NSAccessibility .selectedTextChanged notification.

GTK has no consumer yet and no-ops the action.

See: #9932","state":"closed","html_url":"https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/pull/12902","user":{"login":"jparise","id":10311,"profile_url":"https://github.com/jparise","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/10311?v=4"},"author_association":"CONTRIBUTOR","labels":["os/macos","a11y"],"milestone":"1.4.0","comments":1,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-06-02T23:29:38Z","updated_at":"2026-06-11T00:50:03Z","closed_at":"2026-06-04T18:04:00Z","closed_by":"mitchellh","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

Caveat: the compare endpoint caps its `commits[]` array at 250 entries, so the "last commit in the list" (dated 2026-06-01) is *not* the head — it's the 250th commit. The head's real date is 2026-07-10. `ahead_by`/`total_commits` are not capped and are reliable.

## 2. Backspace keycode encoding — **no upstream issue or PR exists**

Searched issues + PRs (open and closed) for: `backspace keycode encoding`, `backspace DEL 0x7f`, `backspace in:title`, `ghostty_surface_key embedder key encoding`, `libghostty` (all 33 issues / 249 PRs reviewed by title), `keycode` (17 results). **Nothing upstream matches.**

Nearest hits, all non-matching:
- ghostty-org/ghostty#9895 — "macOS: kitty keyboard protocol incorrectly encodes cmd+backspace" — **closed/completed 2025-12-13**, i.e. *before* v1.3.1. About `cmd+backspace` modifier encoding, not the base keycode.
- ghostty-org/ghostty#12226 — "core: implement backarrow key mode (DECBKM) - mode 67" — **closed (unmerged) 2026-04-13**.
- Discussion #5818 "Backspace outputs a space instead of deleting characters over SSH" — **answered/closed**, root cause was missing `xterm-ghostty` terminfo on the remote host, not libghostty encoding. https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/5818

Relevant upstream mechanics (from source, not an issue):

`ghostty_input_key_s.keycode` is a **native platform keycode**, resolved by linear scan in `src/apprt/embedded.zig`:

```zig
// We want to get the physical unmapped key to process keybinds.
const physical_key = keycode: for (input.keycodes.entries) |entry| {
    if (entry.native == self.keycode) break :keycode entry.key;
} else .unidentified;
```

`src/input/keycodes.zig` picks the platform column at comptime — `.ios, .macos => 4` (the `Mac` column). The table header is `//   USB     evdev    XKB     Win     Mac` and the relevant rows are:

```
.{ 0x07002a, 0x000e, 0x0016, 0x000e, 0x0033, "Backspace" },
.{ 0x07002b, 0x000f, 0x0017, 0x000f, 0x0030, "Tab" },
.{ 0x07002c, 0x0039, 0x0041, 0x0039, 0x0031, "Space" },
```

So on macOS/iOS libghostty expects `keycode == 0x33` (51, `kVK_Delete`) for Backspace; `0x31` (49) is Space and `0x30` (48) is Tab. A non-matching keycode yields `.unidentified` rather than an error. This mapping is identical at v1.3.1, 35e1a016, and `main` (the header hunk diff shows no change to `keycode`).

---

## 3. Child exit code always 0 — **no upstream issue or PR exists**; the behaviour is by construction

Searched: `exit_code child_exited` (0 results), `command_finished exit code` (1 unrelated), `"exit code" in:title` (0 results), `exit code command surface` (46, none matching), `wait-after-command exit status` (0 results), plus `search_commits repo:ghostty-org/ghostty exit_code` (25 commits, none a fix for this).

The upstream source explains the symptom. `ghostty_action_command_finished_s.exit_code` is **not** the child process exit status — it is read from the shell's OSC 133;D report, defaulting to `0`:

`src/termio/stream_handler.zig` (main, ~line 1002):
```zig
// bytes, so we just do our best here.
const code: u8 = code: {
    const raw: i32 = cmd.readOption(.exit_code) orelse 0;
    break :code std.math.cast(u8, raw) orelse 1;
};

self.surfaceMessageWriter(.{ .stop_command = code });
```

`src/Surface.zig` then forwards it verbatim into the action (`.stop_command => |v| ... .exit_code = v`). Because `v` is a non-optional `u8`, the `?u8` in `apprt.action.CommandFinished` is never `null`, so the documented sentinel in `include/ghostty.h` is unreachable via this path:

```c
// apprt.action.CommandFinished.C
typedef struct {
  // -1 if no exit code was reported, otherwise 0-255
  int16_t exit_code;
  // number of nanoseconds that command was running for
  uint64_t duration;
} ghostty_action_command_finished_s;
```
```zig
pub fn cval(self: CommandFinished) C {
    return .{ .exit_code = self.exit_code orelse -1, ... };
}
```

The **real** child exit status travels on a different channel — `ghostty_surface_message_childexited_s` / `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SHOW_CHILD_EXITED`, sourced from `xev.Process.WaitError!u32` in `src/termio/Exec.zig`:
```zig
fn processExitCommon(td: *termio.Termio.ThreadData, exit_code: u32) void {
    ...
    _ = td.surface_mailbox.push(.{
        .child_exited = .{ .exit_code = exit_code, .runtime_ms = runtime_ms },
    }, .{ .forever = {} });
}
```

State: **identical in v1.3.1, 35e1a016, and current `main`** — the `command_finished` feature landed in ghostty-org/ghostty#8992 ("core: add 'command finished' notifications", **merged 2025-10-03**), well before v1.3.1, and `ghostty_action_command_finished_s` is byte-identical across both refs (question 8 diff shows no change).

```zig
.show_desktop_notification => |v| {

```

## 8. API drift in `include/ghostty.h`: v1.3.1 → 35e1a016

**Yes, it changed.** 1178 → 1209 lines. Diffed with `GHOSTTY_API` normalized away and whitespace-insensitive: exactly **7 hunks**. Most of the raw 334-line diff is pure noise from prefixing every declaration with the new `GHOSTTY_API` macro.

### A. Build/portability plumbing (source-compatible, no ABI impact)

1. **New `GHOSTTY_API` visibility macro** + Windows/MSVC support:
```c
#ifdef _MSC_VER
#include <BaseTsd.h>
typedef SSIZE_T ssize_t;
#else
#include <sys/types.h>
#endif
```
```c
#ifndef GHOSTTY_API
#if defined(GHOSTTY_STATIC)
  #define GHOSTTY_API
#elif defined(_WIN32) || defined(_WIN64)
  #ifdef GHOSTTY_BUILD_SHARED
    #define GHOSTTY_API __declspec(dllexport)
  #else
    #define GHOSTTY_API __declspec(dllimport)
  #endif
#elif defined(__GNUC__) && __GNUC__ >= 4
  #define GHOSTTY_API __attribute__((visibility("default")))
#else

#endif
#endif
```

# Upstream research: ghostty-org/ghostty + Lakr233/libghostty-spm

## 1. Commit 35e1a016 — date and position relative to v1.3.1

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| SHA | `35e1a0160c4f6797e1bb1ef8e7a2b8c6b114ab58` |
| Date | **2026-07-10T03:04:02Z** (author + committer) |
| Subject | `build(deps): bump cachix/install-nix-action from 31.10.6 to 31.10.7 (#13271)` |
| Author | mitchellh (merge of a dependabot PR) |
| Relation to v1.3.1 | **Descendant** — `status: "ahead"`, `behind_by: 0` |
| Commits ahead | **1,320** |

Citation: `GET /repos/ghostty-org/ghostty/compare/v1.3.1...35e1a016` → `{"status":"ahead","ahead_by":1320,"behind_by":0,"total_commits":1320}`. Commit page: https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/commit/35e1a0160c4f6797e1bb1ef8e7a2b8c6b114ab58

Caveat: the compare endpoint caps its `commits[]` array at 250 entries, so the "last commit in the list" (dated 2026-06-01) is *not* the head — it's the 250th commit. The head's real date is 2026-07-10. `ahead_by`/`total_commits` are not capped and are reliable.

Note: 35e1a016 is a dependency-bump merge commit, i.e. an arbitrary point on `main`, not a release boundary.

---

## 2. Backspace keycode encoding — **no upstream issue or PR exists**

Searched issues + PRs (open and closed) for: `backspace keycode encoding`, `backspace DEL 0x7f`, `backspace in:title`, `ghostty_surface_key embedder key encoding`, `libghostty` (all 33 issues / 249 PRs reviewed by title), `keycode` (17 results). **Nothing upstream matches.**

Nearest hits, all non-matching:
- ghostty-org/ghostty#9895 — "macOS: kitty keyboard protocol incorrectly encodes cmd+backspace" — **closed/completed 2025-12-13**, i.e. *before* v1.3.1. About `cmd+backspace` modifier encoding, not the base keycode.
- ghostty-org/ghostty#12226 — "core: implement backarrow key mode (DECBKM) - mode 67" — **closed (unmerged) 2026-04-13**.
- Discussion #5818 "Backspace outputs a space instead of deleting characters over SSH" — **answered/closed**, root cause was missing `xterm-ghostty` terminfo on the remote host, not libghostty encoding. https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/5818

Relevant upstream mechanics (from source, not an issue):

`ghostty_input_key_s.keycode` is a **native platform keycode**, resolved by linear scan in `src/apprt/embedded.zig`:

```zig
// We want to get the physical unmapped key to process keybinds.
const physical_key = keycode: for (input.keycodes.entries) |entry| {
    if (entry.native == self.keycode) break :keycode entry.key;
} else .unidentified;
```

`src/input/keycodes.zig` picks the platform column at comptime — `.ios, .macos => 4` (the `Mac` column). The table header is `//   USB     evdev    XKB     Win     Mac` and the relevant rows are:

```
.{ 0x07002a, 0x000e, 0x0016, 0x000e, 0x0033, "Backspace" },
.{ 0x07002b, 0x000f, 0x0017, 0x000f, 0x0030, "Tab" },
.{ 0x07002c, 0x0039, 0x0041, 0x0039, 0x0031, "Space" },
```

So on macOS/iOS libghostty expects `keycode == 0x33` (51, `kVK_Delete`) for Backspace; `0x31` (49) is Space and `0x30` (48) is Tab. A non-matching keycode yields `.unidentified` rather than an error. This mapping is identical at v1.3.1, 35e1a016, and `main` (the header hunk diff shows no change to `keycode`).

---

## 3. Child exit code always 0 — **no upstream issue or PR exists**; the behaviour is by construction

Searched: `exit_code child_exited` (0 results), `command_finished exit code` (1 unrelated), `"exit code" in:title` (0 results), `exit code command surface` (46, none matching), `wait-after-command exit status` (0 results), plus `search_commits repo:ghostty-org/ghostty exit_code` (25 commits, none a fix for this).

The upstream source explains the symptom. `ghostty_action_command_finished_s.exit_code` is **not** the child process exit status — it is read from the shell's OSC 133;D report, defaulting to `0`:

`src/termio/stream_handler.zig` (main, ~line 1002):
```zig
// bytes, so we just do our best here.
const code: u8 = code: {
    const raw: i32 = cmd.readOption(.exit_code) orelse 0;
    break :code std.math.cast(u8, raw) orelse 1;
};

self.surfaceMessageWriter(.{ .stop_command = code });
```

`src/Surface.zig` then forwards it verbatim into the action (`.stop_command => |v| ... .exit_code = v`). Because `v` is a non-optional `u8`, the `?u8` in `apprt.action.CommandFinished` is never `null`, so the documented sentinel in `include/ghostty.h` is unreachable via this path:

```c
// apprt.action.CommandFinished.C
typedef struct {
  // -1 if no exit code was reported, otherwise 0-255
  int16_t exit_code;
  // number of nanoseconds that command was running for
  uint64_t duration;
} ghostty_action_command_finished_s;
```
```zig
pub fn cval(self: CommandFinished) C {
    return .{ .exit_code = self.exit_code orelse -1, ... };
}
```

The **real** child exit status travels on a different channel — `ghostty_surface_message_childexited_s` / `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SHOW_CHILD_EXITED`, sourced from `xev.Process.WaitError!u32` in `src/termio/Exec.zig`:
```zig
fn processExitCommon(td: *termio.Termio.ThreadData, exit_code: u32) void {
    ...
    _ = td.surface_mailbox.push(.{
        .child_exited = .{ .exit_code = exit_code, .runtime_ms = runtime_ms },
    }, .{ .forever = {} });
}
```

State: **identical in v1.3.1, 35e1a016, and current `main`** — the `command_finished` feature landed in ghostty-org/ghostty#8992 ("core: add 'command finished' notifications", **merged 2025-10-03**), well before v1.3.1, and `ghostty_action_command_finished_s` is byte-identical across both refs (question 8 diff shows no change).

---

## 4. Ctrl-Tab — **no upstream issue or PR about libghostty failing to encode it**

All four Ctrl+Tab issues are closed and predate v1.3.1 by a wide margin; none concern libghostty/embedder byte encoding:

| # | Title | State | Closed |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#7051](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/issues/7051) | macOS: input `ctrl+tab` doesn't register | closed / completed | 2025-04-10 |
| [#2192](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/issues/2192) | Stack-like ctrl-tab and ctrl-shift-tab behaviour | closed / completed | 2024-10-06 |
| [#1257](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/issues/1257) | `ctrl+tab` key binding acting odd when new config is reloaded | closed / completed | 2024-01-08 |
| [#957](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/issues/957) | ctrl+tab keybinds aren't working | closed / completed | 2023-11-24 |

#7051 is the closest but is about macOS delivering the event at all, not encoding — mitchellh's note in the body: *"I'm not seeing any input event at all on the macOS side when following the instructions above, on tip."* It is scoped to the macOS system "App Shortcuts" preference intercepting Ctrl+Tab before the app sees it, labelled `os/macos` + `input`, and was closed as completed the same day it was filed (2025-04-10).

No open or closed issue/PR mentions Ctrl+Tab producing zero bytes under the kitty keyboard protocol / enhanced modes.

**Issue [#5634](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/issues/5634)** — "OSC 99 style desktop notifications"

## 8. API drift in `include/ghostty.h`: v1.3.1 → 35e1a016

**Yes, it changed.** 1178 → 1209 lines. Diffed with `GHOSTTY_API` normalized away and whitespace-insensitive: exactly **7 hunks**. Most of the raw 334-line diff is pure noise from prefixing every declaration with the new `GHOSTTY_API` macro.

### A. Build/portability plumbing (source-compatible, no ABI impact)

1. **New `GHOSTTY_API` visibility macro** + Windows/MSVC support:
```c
#ifdef _MSC_VER
#include <BaseTsd.h>
typedef SSIZE_T ssize_t;
#else
#include <sys/types.h>
#endif
```
```c
#ifndef GHOSTTY_API
#if defined(GHOSTTY_STATIC)
  #define GHOSTTY_API
#elif defined(_WIN32) || defined(_WIN64)
  #ifdef GHOSTTY_BUILD_SHARED
    #define GHOSTTY_API __declspec(dllexport)
  #else
    #define GHOSTTY_API __declspec(dllimport)
  #endif
#elif defined(__GNUC__) && __GNUC__ >= 4
  #define GHOSTTY_API __attribute__((visibility("default")))
#else
  #define GHOSTTY_API
#endif
#endif
```
Every published function is now `GHOSTTY_API`-prefixed. On Apple/clang this expands to `__attribute__((visibility("default")))` — no mangling or calling-convention change.

### B. ⚠️ `ghostty_action_e` enum RENUMBERED — the headline ABI break

```diff
   GHOSTTY_ACTION_RING_BELL,
+  GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED,
   GHOSTTY_ACTION_UNDO,
```

`GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` is inserted **mid-enum**, not appended. Every subsequent tag shifts by +1:

`UNDO`, `REDO`, `CHECK_FOR_UPDATES`, `OPEN_URL`, **`SHOW_CHILD_EXITED`**, `PROGRESS_REPORT`, `SHOW_ON_SCREEN_KEYBOARD`, **`COMMAND_FINISHED`**, `START_SEARCH`, `END_SEARCH`, `SEARCH_TOTAL`, `SEARCH_SELECTED`, `READONLY`, `COPY_TITLE_TO_CLIPBOARD`.

Directly relevant to questions 3 and 5: any embedder that hardcodes, persists, or bridges these tag values numerically (rather than re-importing the header) will mis-dispatch `SHOW_CHILD_EXITED` and `COMMAND_FINISHED` after the bump. Provenance: ghostty-org/ghostty#12902 "core: send selection_changed notification" (**merged 2026-06-04**).

### C. Functions REMOVED (1)

```diff
-bool ghostty_app_key_is_binding(ghostty_app_t, ghostty_input_key_s);
```
Hard link-time break. Replaced by (B below). Provenance: commit [`4ceeba48`](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/commit/4ceeba4851030e75398cf1e5d3f7d8c7ed645e87) — "config: use Config to check key binding instead of App (**#12415**)", merged **2026-04-24**:
> "Previously `ghostty_app_key_is_binding` (unlike Surface) is just using `config.keybind` to check whether a KeyEvent is in the set or not. … I didn't find any usages of this in GTK, so it shouldn't affect anything."

### D. Functions ADDED (3)

```diff
+bool ghostty_config_key_is_binding(ghostty_config_t, ghostty_input_key_s);
```
Replacement for C — note the **receiver type changed from `ghostty_app_t` to `ghostty_config_t`**.

```diff
+uint64_t ghostty_surface_foreground_pid(ghostty_surface_t);
+ghostty_string_s ghostty_surface_tty_name(ghostty_surface_t);
```
Purely additive. Satisfies open issue [#12065](https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/issues/12065) "macOS GhosttyKit: expose child PID / TTY on `ghostty_surface_t`" (still open). `ghostty_surface_tty_name` returns `ghostty_string_s` → caller must `ghostty_string_free`.

### E. Union member REMOVED

```diff
 typedef union {
-  ghostty_input_key_e translated;
   ghostty_input_key_e physical;
   uint32_t unicode;
   // catch_all has no payload
 } ghostty_input_trigger_key_u;
```
`ghostty_input_trigger_key_u.translated` deleted. Source-breaking for anyone reading `.translated`; no size change (`translated` and `physical` were the same type, and `GHOSTTY_TRIGGER_PHYSICAL/UNICODE/CATCH_ALL` in `ghostty_input_trigger_tag_e` are unchanged).

### F. `ghostty_ipc_action_tag_e` extended (appended — safe)

```diff
 typedef enum {
   GHOSTTY_IPC_ACTION_NEW_WINDOW,
+  GHOSTTY_IPC_ACTION_TOGGLE_QUICK_TERMINAL,
 } ghostty_ipc_action_tag_e;
```

### G. What did NOT change

- `ghostty_action_s` / `ghostty_action_u` — **no union members added, removed, renamed, or reordered.** (`SELECTION_CHANGED` carries no payload.)
- `ghostty_action_command_finished_s` — unchanged (`int16_t exit_code; uint64_t duration;`).

# CMT-2 review verdict + libghostty pin bump to 1.3.2

## Context

`TODOS.md:10` ("Own the GhosttyKit xcframework — CMT-2") sits in **P1 — before GA** and gates the
other P1 item (CMT-3, terminal content a11y, `TODOS.md:70`). It was reviewed to confirm it is still
needed. **It is not needed as written** — its two load-bearing factual claims are wrong, and the
value it promises is available today from a version bump.

### What the entry claims vs. what is true (verified 2026-08-05)

| Claim in TODOS.md | Reality |
|---|---|
| "libghostty-spm is still on 1.2.3 … trailing ghostty by ~2 versions on a single maintainer's cadence" (`:31-34`) | **Package version ≠ ghostty version.** libghostty-spm 1.2.3 was built from ghostty ref **`v1.3.1`** (`332b2aef`) — the newest ghostty *release* tag. We are not behind; we are on the newest release engine. |
| "tags 1.2.1→1.2.3 only" (`:33`) | Tags now run 1.2.1→1.2.11, 1.3.0, 1.3.1, **1.3.2** (2026-07-27). Releases are automated (`github-actions[bot]`, weekly cron Mon 06:23 UTC). Packages 1.2.10+ build from ghostty **main** (`35e1a016`, 2026-07-10, **1320 commits ahead of v1.3.1**). |
| "Everything we'll want next (OSC 99 etc.) lives upstream of any release — only the owner-of-the-pin path can reach it" (`:35-36`) | False both ways. *Merged* main-branch changes arrive weekly via the packager. And OSC 99 is **not reachable even with a fork**: PR #10467 adds only a parser, and its one-line `stream.zig` change puts `.kitty_desktop_notification` in the **"unimplemented OSC callback → log and discard"** branch. Its own body: *"This includes only parsing of the OSC. You cannot (yet) use OSC 99 to send notifications."* Three further pieces (stream dispatch, an apprt action, a `ghostty_action_*` tag) do not exist as open or merged PRs. Issue #5634 is milestone **1.4.0**. The plan step "confirm OSC 99 fires" would fail. |
| CMT-3: "ghostty upstream has merged a11y plumbing we'd want to ride — #12902 … post-upgrade it comes from the engine" (`:88-93`) | #12902 **merged 2026-06-04** and is in the main build the packager already ships: `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` is present in `include/ghostty.h` at `35e1a016`. CMT-3 is unblocked by a **pin bump**, not by owning the build. |

### What survives — and is understated

Supply chain is the one real argument, and the entry undersells it. The shipped binary is **not
stock ghostty**: `Patches/ghostty/` in libghostty-spm carries **11 patches (~200 KB)** applied at
build time, including `0002-host-managed-io.patch` (~18 KB, changes how IO/PTY is hosted) and
`0003-prebuilt-framedata.patch` (113 KB). The artifact is **checksummed but not signed or
notarized** (SPM SHA-256 only — ghostty-org minisigns its own artifacts). arm64e slices shipped and
were rolled back mid-July (1.3.2 re-cut). That is what we embed in a notarized app, in the component
that runs the user's shell. It is a GA-time decision, not a feature blocker.

Also: ghostty-org **does** now publish an official minisigned `ghostty-vt.xcframework` (PR #12149) —
but that is **libghostty-vt** (VT parsing only), a different library from the apprt embedding API
`GhosttyKit` wraps. It is not a replacement. The apprt header still declares itself internal
("The only consumer of this API is the macOS app"), byte-identical at v1.3.1 and main, and
embedder-facing requests are being closed `not_planned` (#12111, #12110, #12112, #12086, #12657).

### Why the bump is the actual win

`include/ghostty.h` between `v1.3.1` (what we ship) and `35e1a016` (what 1.3.2 ships):

- **Added** `ghostty_surface_foreground_pid` + `ghostty_surface_tty_name` — precisely the limitation
  recorded at `macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:95-97` ("libghostty exposes no PTY
  child PID for `proc_pidinfo`", CMT-1).
- **Added** `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` — CMT-3's a11y hook.
- **Removed** `ghostty_app_key_is_binding` and `ghostty_input_trigger_key_u.translated` — **we call
  neither** (verified by grep over `macapp/WorkroomApp/`), so there is no link-time break.
- `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` is inserted **mid-enum**, renumbering 14 following tags
  including `SHOW_CHILD_EXITED` and `COMMAND_FINISHED`. We dispatch on symbolic constants
  re-imported from the header, so this is compile-safe — but it is invisible at compile time, which
  is exactly why it needs behavioural retest, not just a green build.
- Everything else we consume (61 `ghostty_*` symbols, 41 `GHOSTTY_*` constants) is unchanged apart
  from a new `GHOSTTY_API` visibility macro prefix (no ABI effect on Apple/clang).

Plus 1320 commits of upstream fixes that may obsolete two shipped workarounds.

## Work

### 1. Bump the pin

- `macapp/project.yml:55` — `exactVersion: 1.2.3` → `1.3.2`. Update the comment block above it
  (`:49-53`): keep "pin EXACT", **record the ghostty sha the package builds from**
  (`35e1a0160c4f6797e1bb1ef8e7a2b8c6b114ab58`), and note the collision hazard that package `1.3.1`
  ≠ ghostty `v1.3.1`. Replace the "Pre-GA we move to a self-built xcframework" line with a pointer
  to the rewritten CMT-2.
- Regenerate + resolve: `make app-generate`, then `xcodebuild -resolvePackageDependencies` (or a
  clean `make app-build`). `macapp/DerivedData/SourcePackages` holds the old checkout;
  `Package.resolved` is gitignored, so the pin in `project.yml` is the only tracked source of truth.
- CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:151-163` keys the SPM cache on `hashFiles('macapp/project.yml')`, so
  the bump invalidates it once by design. `nightly.yml` / `release.yml` resolve cold — nothing to do.

### 2. Build and fix fallout

Expect none. If the build breaks, the candidates are the two removed symbols (we use neither) and
the `GHOSTTY_API` prefix (no source effect). `GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.handleAction`
(`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttyRuntimeAdapter.swift:25`) has a `default:` arm, so the new action
tag needs no code change to be safe — leave `SELECTION_CHANGED` unhandled in this change; wiring it
is CMT-3's job.

### 3. Behavioural retest of the renumbered action tags

The enum shift is the only real risk in this change. Exercise every tag we dispatch, since a
mis-dispatch is silent (`default:` returns false):

- `COMMAND_FINISHED` / `SHOW_CHILD_EXITED` → run-tab status. `macapp/WorkroomAppUITests/RunStatusUITests.swift`
  covers the non-zero-exit path; the supervisor status file (`macapp/Resources/run-supervisor/supervisor.sh:103`)
  is authoritative, so also confirm `AppStore.markRunExited` (`Core/AppStore.swift:2118-2144`) still agrees.
- `PWD` → ⌘-click path resolution; `SET_TITLE` → tab titles; `PROGRESS_REPORT` → the busy indicator
  (OSC 9;4); `DESKTOP_NOTIFICATION` → OSC 9/777 notifications; `SCROLLBAR` → the scrollbar overlay;
  `RING_BELL`; `START_SEARCH`/`END_SEARCH`/`SEARCH_TOTAL`/`SEARCH_SELECTED` → scrollback search.

### 4. Re-verify the workarounds this may obsolete

Test, don't assume — and **do not delete anything in this change**. Each removal is its own commit
with its own evidence, or a TODO entry if it survives:

- **Backspace DEL-as-text** (`Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:900-906`, `filterSpecialCharacters:1158-1163`,
  pinned by `WorkroomAppTests/GhosttySurfaceViewTests.swift:36-40`). Note for whoever tests it: there
  is **no upstream issue for this**, and upstream's `src/input/keycodes.zig` maps macOS keycode
  `0x33` → Backspace, which is what AppKit reports. So the symptom may be an artifact of the
  packager's patch set rather than stock ghostty — worth a raw-PTY byte probe either way.
- **Search wrap synthesized host-side** (`Core/TerminalSearch.swift:63-66`).
- **⌃Tab sends no bytes** (memory-confirmed on 1.2.3; `AppShortcutReservationTests` pins Tab as
  never-reserved). No upstream issue exists; re-probe on the new engine.

### 5. Correct the record

- `TODOS.md:10-68` — rewrite CMT-2: strike the packager-lag and OSC-99 rationales, state the
  package-vs-ghostty versioning trap explicitly (it is what caused the error), and re-argue it on
  the patch set + unsigned artifact. Demote from "P1 before GA" to a **GA-time supply-chain
  decision**, since no feature now depends on it.
- `TODOS.md:88-93` — CMT-3: replace "sequence with the xcframework upgrade" with "unblocked by the
  1.3.2 pin; `GHOSTTY_ACTION_SELECTION_CHANGED` is available".
- New TODO entry: **regenerate `macapp/Resources/ghostty/`** (terminfo + shell-integration) from
  `35e1a016` and record that sha. `macapp/Resources/ghostty/SOURCE.md` currently says "Sourced from
  a recent Ghostty build" with no ref, and its closing line ("Themes are intentionally omitted") is
  factually stale — `themes/` was added by `8fd7fa19`/`602b5aa3` and is load-bearing for the theme
  picker. Fix the stale sentence now; the regeneration is the separate item. (libghostty-spm PR #43,
  open, proposes shipping these from the package — worth watching rather than racing.)
- Version strings in prose: `macapp/CLAUDE.md` (Gotchas → "pinned `exactVersion: 1.2.3`"),
  `macapp/README.md:141-143`, root `README.md:120` ("libghostty-spm 1.2.x").
- `macapp/QA-libghostty.md:73-80` (§H) — the OSC 99 note should record that #10467 alone is
  insufficient, so nobody re-derives this.

## Verification

Build and test targets need the sandbox disabled (`make app-*` cannot run sandboxed):

1. `make app-build` — must compile with no changes to call sites.
2. `make app-test` — read pass/fail from the `.xcresult` via `xcresulttool`; the Xcode 26 console
   summary is unreliable.
3. Targeted UI test for the exit-code path (own scheme; `make app-uitest` ignores `APP_TEST_FLAGS`,
   so call `xcodebuild` directly with `-only-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/RunStatusUITests`).
4. `make app-run`, then walk `macapp/QA-libghostty.md` A–M by hand — it is the checklist written for
   exactly this engine swap. Minimum: §A resources fail-soft, §G bell, §H OSC 9/777 notification,
   §M search wrap, plus backspace over a real shell and ⌃Tab into a TUI.
5. Confirm no orphaned shells after repeated workroom switch/delete (`ps`), per
   `macapp/README.md:144-146` — surface teardown is the historical crash site.
6. `make app-lint` before committing.

Rollback is one line: revert `exactVersion` to `1.2.3`.

## AskUserQuestion Format

### Tool resolution (read first)

"AskUserQuestion" can resolve to two tools at runtime: the **host MCP variant** (e.g. `mcp__conductor__AskUserQuestion` — appears in your tool list when the host registers it) or the **native** Claude Code tool.

**Conductor rule (read before the MCP rule):** if `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` was echoed by the preamble, do NOT call AskUserQuestion at all — neither native nor any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant. Render EVERY decision brief as the **prose form** below and STOP. This is proactive, not a reaction to a failure: Conductor disables native AUQ and its MCP variant is flaky (it returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`), so prose is the reliable path. **Auto-decide preferences still apply first:** if a `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` result has already surfaced for a question, proceed with that option (no prose). Because in Conductor you go straight to prose without ever calling the tool, this auto-decide-first ordering is enforced HERE, not only by the PreToolUse hook. When you render a Conductor prose brief, also capture it with `bin/gstack-question-log` (the PostToolUse capture hook never fires on a prose path, so `/plan-tune` history/learning depends on this call).

**Rule (non-Conductor):** if any `mcp__*__AskUserQuestion` variant is in your tool list, prefer it. Hosts may disable native AUQ via `--disallowedTools AskUserQuestion` (Conductor does, by default) and route through their MCP variant; calling native there silently fails. Same questions/options shape; same decision-brief format applies.

If AskUserQuestion is unavailable (no variant in your tool list) OR a call to it fails, do NOT silently auto-decide or write the decision to the plan file as a substitute. Follow the **failure fallback** below.

### When AskUserQuestion is unavailable or a call fails

Tell three outcomes apart:

1. **Auto-decide denial (NOT a failure).** The result contains `[plan-tune auto-decide] <id> → <option>` — the preference hook working as designed. Proceed with that option. Do NOT retry, do NOT fall back to prose.
2. **Genuine failure** — no variant in your tool list, OR the variant is present but the call returns an error / missing result (MCP transport error, empty result, host bug — e.g. Conductor's MCP AskUserQuestion is flaky and returns `[Tool result missing due to internal error]`).
   - If it was present and **errored** (not absent), retry the SAME call **once** — but only if no answer could have surfaced (a missing-result error can arrive after the user already saw the question; retrying would double-prompt, so if it may have reached them, treat as pending, don't retry).
   - Then branch on `SESSION_KIND` (echoed by the preamble; empty/absent ⇒ `interactive`):
     - `spawned` → defer to the **Spawned session** block: auto-choose the recommended option. Never prose, never BLOCKED.
     - `headless` → `BLOCKED — AskUserQuestion unavailable`; stop and wait (no human can answer).
     - `interactive` → **prose fallback** (below).

**Prose fallback — render the decision brief as a markdown message, not a tool call.** Same information as the tool format below, different structure (paragraphs, not ✅/❌ bullets). It MUST surface this triad:

1. **A clear ELI10 of the issue itself** — plain English on what's being decided and why it matters (the question, not per-choice), naming the stakes. Lead with it.
2. **Completeness scores per choice** — explicit `Completeness: X/10` on EACH choice (10 complete, 7 happy-path, 3 shortcut); use the kind-note when options differ in kind not coverage, but never silently drop the score.
3. **The recommendation and why** — a `Recommendation: <choice> because <reason>` line plus the `(recommended)` marker on that choice.

Layout: a `D<N>` title + a one-line note to reply with a letter (in Conductor this is the normal path; elsewhere it means AskUserQuestion was unavailable or errored); the issue ELI10; the Recommendation line; then ONE paragraph per choice carrying its `(recommended)` marker, its `Completeness: X/10`, and 2-4 sentences of reasoning — never a bare bullet list; a closing `Net:` line. Split chains / 5+ options: one prose block per per-option call, in sequence. Then STOP and wait — the user's typed answer is the decision. In plan mode this satisfies end-of-turn like a tool call.

**Continuation — mapping a typed reply back to a brief.** Each brief carries a stable label (`D<N>`, or `D<N>.k` in a split chain). The user references it (e.g. "3.2: B"). A bare letter maps to the single most-recent UNANSWERED brief; if more than one is open (a split chain), do NOT guess — ask which `D<N>.k` it answers. Never apply a bare letter ambiguously across a chain.

**One-way / destructive confirmations in prose.** When the decision is a one-way door (irreversible or destructive — delete, force-push, drop, overwrite), prose is a WEAKER gate than the tool, so make it stronger: require an explicit typed confirmation (the exact option letter or word), state plainly what is irreversible, and NEVER proceed on a vague, partial, or ambiguous reply — re-ask instead. Treat silence or "ok"/"sure" without the explicit choice as not-yet-confirmed.

### Format

Every AskUserQuestion is a decision brief and must be sent as tool_use, not prose — unless the documented failure fallback above applies (interactive session + the call is unavailable/erroring), in which case the prose fallback is the correct output.

```
D<N> — <one-line question title>
Project/branch/task: <1 short grounding sentence using _BRANCH>
ELI10: <plain English a 16-year-old could follow, 2-4 sentences, name the stakes>
Stakes if we pick wrong: <one sentence on what breaks, what user sees, what's lost>
Recommendation: <choice> because <one-line reason>
Completeness: A=X/10, B=Y/10   (or: Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score)
Pros / cons:
A) <option label> (recommended)
  ✅ <pro — concrete, observable, ≥40 chars>
  ❌ <con — honest, ≥40 chars>
B) <option label>
  ✅ <pro>
  ❌ <con>
Net: <one-line synthesis of what you're actually trading off>
```

D-numbering: first question in a skill invocation is `D1`; increment yourself. This is a model-level instruction, not a runtime counter.

ELI10 is always present, in plain English, not function names. Recommendation is ALWAYS present. Keep the `(recommended)` label; AUTO_DECIDE depends on it.

Completeness: use `Completeness: N/10` only when options differ in coverage. 10 = complete, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut. If options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.`

Pros / cons: use ✅ and ❌. Minimum 2 pros and 1 con per option when the choice is real; Minimum 40 characters per bullet. Hard-stop escape for one-way/destructive confirmations: `✅ No cons — this is a hard-stop choice`.

Neutral posture: `Recommendation: <default> — this is a taste call, no strong preference either way`; `(recommended)` STAYS on the default option for AUTO_DECIDE.

Effort both-scales: when an option involves effort, label both human-team and CC+gstack time, e.g. `(human: ~2 days / CC: ~15 min)`. Makes AI compression visible at decision time.

Net line closes the tradeoff. Per-skill instructions may add stricter rules.

### Handling 5+ options — split, never drop

AskUserQuestion caps every call at **4 options**. With 5+ real options, NEVER
drop, merge, or silently defer one to fit. Pick a compliant shape:

- **Batch into ≤4-groups** — for coherent alternatives (e.g. version bumps,
  layout variants). One call, 5th surfaced only if first 4 don't fit.
- **Split per-option** — for independent scope items (e.g. "ship E1..E6?").
  Fire N sequential calls, one per option. Default to this when unsure.

Per-option call shape: `D<N>.k` header (e.g. D3.1..D3.5), ELI10 per option,
Recommendation, kind-note (no completeness score — Include/Defer/Cut/Hold are
decision actions), and 4 buckets:
**A) Include**, **B) Defer**, **C) Cut**, **D) Hold** (stop chain, discuss).

After the chain, fire `D<N>.final` to validate the assembled set (reprompt
dependency conflicts) and confirm shipping it. Use `D<N>.revise-<k>` to
revise one option without re-running the chain.

For N>6, fire a `D<N>.0` meta-AskUserQuestion first (proceed / narrow / batch).

question_ids for split chains: `<skill>-split-<option-slug>` (kebab-case ASCII,
≤64 chars, `-2`/`-3` suffix on collision). The runtime checker
(`bin/gstack-question-preference`) refuses `never-ask` on any `*-split-*` id,
so split chains are never AUTO_DECIDE-eligible — the user's option set is sacred.

**Full rule + worked examples + Hold/dependency semantics:** see
`docs/askuserquestion-split.md` in the gstack repo. Read on demand when N>4.

**Non-ASCII characters — write directly, never \u-escape.** When any string
field contains Chinese (繁體/簡體), Japanese, Korean, or other non-ASCII text,
emit the literal UTF-8 characters; never escape them as `\uXXXX` (the pipe is
UTF-8 native, and manual escaping miscodes long CJK strings). Only `\n`,
`\t`, `\"`, `\\` remain allowed. Full rationale + worked example: see
`docs/askuserquestion-cjk.md`. Read on demand when a question contains CJK.

### Self-check before emitting

Before calling AskUserQuestion, verify:
- [ ] D<N> header present
- [ ] ELI10 paragraph present (stakes line too)
- [ ] Recommendation line present with concrete reason
- [ ] Completeness scored (coverage) OR kind-note present (kind)
- [ ] Every option has ≥2 ✅ and ≥1 ❌, each ≥40 chars (or hard-stop escape)
- [ ] (recommended) label on one option (even for neutral-posture)
- [ ] Dual-scale effort labels on effort-bearing options (human / CC)
- [ ] Net line closes the decision
- [ ] You are calling the tool, not writing prose — unless `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` (then prose is the DEFAULT, not the tool) OR the documented failure fallback applies (then: prose with the mandatory triad — issue ELI10, per-choice Completeness, Recommendation + `(recommended)` — and a "reply with a letter" instruction, then STOP)
- [ ] Non-ASCII characters (CJK / accents) written directly, NOT \u-escaped
- [ ] If you had 5+ options, you split (or batched into ≤4-groups) — did NOT drop any
- [ ] If you split, you checked dependencies between options before firing the chain
- [ ] If a per-option Hold fires, you stopped the chain immediately (didn't queue)


## Artifacts Sync (skill start)

```bash
_GSTACK_HOME="${GSTACK_HOME:-$HOME/.gstack}"
# Prefer the v1.27.0.0 artifacts file; fall back to brain file for users
# upgrading mid-stream before the migration script runs.
if [ -f "$HOME/.gstack-artifacts-remote.txt" ]; then
  _BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE="$HOME/.gstack-artifacts-remote.txt"
else
  _BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE="$HOME/.gstack-brain-remote.txt"
fi
_BRAIN_SYNC_BIN="~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-brain-sync"
_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN="~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-config"

# /sync-gbrain context-load: teach the agent to use gbrain when it's available.
# Per-worktree pin: post-spike redesign uses kubectl-style `.gbrain-source` in the
# git toplevel to scope queries. Look for the pin in the worktree (not a global
# state file) so that opening worktree B without a pin doesn't claim "indexed"
# just because worktree A was synced. Empty string when gbrain is not
# configured (zero context cost for non-gbrain users).
_GBRAIN_CONFIG="$HOME/.gbrain/config.json"
if [ -f "$_GBRAIN_CONFIG" ] && command -v gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  _GBRAIN_VERSION_OK=$(gbrain --version 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^gbrain ' || echo 0)
  if [ "$_GBRAIN_VERSION_OK" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH=""
    _REPO_TOP=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if [ -n "$_REPO_TOP" ] && [ -f "$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source" ]; then
      _GBRAIN_PIN_PATH="$_REPO_TOP/.gbrain-source"
    fi
    if [ -n "$_GBRAIN_PIN_PATH" ]; then
      echo "GBrain configured. Prefer \`gbrain search\`/\`gbrain query\` over Grep for"
      echo "semantic questions; use \`gbrain code-def\`/\`code-refs\`/\`code-callers\` for"
      echo "symbol-aware code lookup. See \"## GBrain Search Guidance\" in CLAUDE.md."
      echo "Run /sync-gbrain to refresh."
    else
      echo "GBrain configured but this worktree isn't pinned yet. Run \`/sync-gbrain --full\`"
      echo "before relying on \`gbrain search\` for code questions in this worktree."
      echo "Falls back to Grep until pinned."
    fi
  fi
fi

_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE=$("$_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN" get artifacts_sync_mode 2>/dev/null || echo off)

# Detect remote-MCP mode (Path 4 of /setup-gbrain). Local artifacts sync is
# a no-op in remote mode; the brain server pulls from GitHub/GitLab on its
# own cadence. Read claude.json directly to keep this preamble fast (no
# subprocess to claude CLI on every skill start).
_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="none"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -f "$HOME/.claude.json" ]; then
  _GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE=$(jq -r '.mcpServers.gbrain.type // .mcpServers.gbrain.transport // empty' "$HOME/.claude.json" 2>/dev/null)
  case "$_GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE" in
    url|http|sse) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="remote-http" ;;
    stdio) _GBRAIN_MCP_MODE="local-stdio" ;;
  esac
fi

if [ -f "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" ] && [ ! -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" = "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_NEW_URL=$(head -1 "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')
  if [ -n "$_BRAIN_NEW_URL" ]; then
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: artifacts repo detected: $_BRAIN_NEW_URL"
    echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: run 'gstack-brain-restore' to pull your cross-machine artifacts (or 'gstack-config set artifacts_sync_mode off' to dismiss forever)"
  fi
fi

if [ -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" != "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE="$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-last-pull"
  _BRAIN_NOW=$(date +%s)
  _BRAIN_DO_PULL=1
  if [ -f "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE" ]; then
    _BRAIN_LAST=$(cat "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    _BRAIN_AGE=$(( _BRAIN_NOW - _BRAIN_LAST ))
    [ "$_BRAIN_AGE" -lt 86400 ] && _BRAIN_DO_PULL=0
  fi
  if [ "$_BRAIN_DO_PULL" = "1" ]; then
    ( cd "$_GSTACK_HOME" && git fetch origin >/dev/null 2>&1 && git merge --ff-only "origin/$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)" >/dev/null 2>&1 ) || true
    echo "$_BRAIN_NOW" > "$_BRAIN_LAST_PULL_FILE"
  fi
  "$_BRAIN_SYNC_BIN" --once 2>/dev/null || true
fi

if [ "$_GBRAIN_MCP_MODE" = "remote-http" ]; then
  # Remote-MCP mode: local artifacts sync is a no-op (brain admin's server
  # pulls from GitHub/GitLab). Show the user this is by design, not broken.
  _GBRAIN_HOST=$(jq -r '.mcpServers.gbrain.url // empty' "$HOME/.claude.json" 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's|^https?://([^/:]+).*|\1|')
  echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: remote-mode (managed by brain server ${_GBRAIN_HOST:-remote})"
elif [ -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" != "off" ]; then
  _BRAIN_QUEUE_DEPTH=0
  [ -f "$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-queue.jsonl" ] && _BRAIN_QUEUE_DEPTH=$(wc -l < "$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-queue.jsonl" | tr -d ' ')
  _BRAIN_LAST_PUSH="never"
  [ -f "$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-last-push" ] && _BRAIN_LAST_PUSH=$(cat "$_GSTACK_HOME/.brain-last-push" 2>/dev/null || echo never)
  echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: mode=$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE | last_push=$_BRAIN_LAST_PUSH | queue=$_BRAIN_QUEUE_DEPTH"
else
  echo "ARTIFACTS_SYNC: off"
fi
```

## Model-Specific Behavioral Patch (claude)

The following nudges are tuned for the claude model family. They are
**subordinate** to skill workflow, STOP points, AskUserQuestion gates, plan-mode
safety, and /ship review gates. If a nudge below conflicts with skill instructions,
the skill wins. Treat these as preferences, not rules.

**Todo-list discipline.** When working through a multi-step plan, mark each task
complete individually as you finish it. Do not batch-complete at the end. If a task
turns out to be unnecessary, mark it skipped with a one-line reason.

**Think before heavy actions.** For complex operations (refactors, migrations,
non-trivial new features), briefly state your approach before executing. This lets
the user course-correct cheaply instead of mid-flight.

**Dedicated tools over Bash.** Prefer Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep over shell
equivalents (cat, sed, find, grep). The dedicated tools are cheaper and clearer.

## Voice

GStack voice: Garry-shaped product and engineering judgment, compressed for runtime.

- Lead with the point. Say what it does, why it matters, and what changes for the builder.
- Be concrete. Name files, functions, line numbers, commands, outputs, evals, and real numbers.
- Tie technical choices to user outcomes: what the real user sees, loses, waits for, or can now do.
- Be direct about quality. Bugs matter. Edge cases matter. Fix the whole thing, not the demo path.
- Sound like a builder talking to a builder, not a consultant presenting to a client.
- Never corporate, academic, PR, or hype. Avoid filler, throat-clearing, generic optimism, and founder cosplay.
- No em dashes. No AI vocabulary: delve, crucial, robust, comprehensive, nuanced, multifaceted, furthermore, moreover, additionally, pivotal, landscape, tapestry, underscore, foster, showcase, intricate, vibrant, fundamental, significant.
- The user has context you do not: domain knowledge, timing, relationships, taste. Cross-model agreement is a recommendation, not a decision. The user decides.

Good: "auth.ts:47 returns undefined when the session cookie expires. Users hit a white screen. Fix: add a null check and redirect to /login. Two lines."
Bad: "I've identified a potential issue in the authentication flow that may cause problems under certain conditions."

## Completeness Principle — Boil the Ocean

AI makes completeness cheap, so the complete thing is the goal. Recommend full coverage (tests, edge cases, error paths) — boil the ocean one lake at a time. The only thing out of scope is genuinely unrelated work (rewrites, multi-quarter migrations); flag that as separate scope, never as an excuse for a shortcut.

When options differ in coverage, include `Completeness: X/10` (10 = all edge cases, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut). When options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.` Do not fabricate scores.

For high-stakes ambiguity (architecture, data model, destructive scope, missing context), STOP. Name it in one sentence, present 2-3 options with tradeoffs, and ask. Do not use for routine coding or obvious changes.
